newsitem.title: CHINA: China eyes grain exports in second half of 1997.
newsitem.headline: China eyes grain exports in second half of 1997.

text.p: The second half of 1997 could be an opportune time for China to export grain, the Grain and Oil Market Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Thursday.

"China lost the best opportunity to export grain, especially corn, in 1996...due to falling international prices," it quoted Li Kewei of the Agriculture Ministry's market information department as saying.
"We need to wait for the coming of the next best opportunity. This opportunity could come in the second half of 1997," Li said without elaborating.
Guo Beixing, of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, proposed resuming grain exports after a bountiful harvest in 1996.

Xie Yang, an official of the cabinet's Development Research Centre, suggested lowering domestic corn prices and shipping a proportion of northeast China's corn output to southern China for every tonne of corn exported, the newspaper said.
Corn supply in northeast China outstrips demand due to a stable harvest in 1996, but south China's feed industry was in need of corn, Xie said.
Xie said the domestic grain market would not be drastically affected if China's net grain exports did not exceed 2.0 million tonnes a year.
